text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv said on Monday cost cutting and improved group synergies were behind a 14 percent increase in profits for the first nine months of the year.
"The improvement is largely explained by a higher degree of integration and continued savings," Autoliv said in a statement.

Autoliv, which recently announced a merger with the car safety division of U.S.-based Morton International, posted a profit after financial items of 863 million crowns ($131.2 million), up from the 758 million shown in the same period last year.
Sales increased by 10 percent during the period to 8.55 billion crowns. Autoliv said sales had been hit by the stronger crown and bolstered by acquisitions.

"Changes in currency exchange rates have reduced sales by 10 percent, whilst company acquisitions have had a positive effect of nine percent. Underlying sales growth was thus 11 percent," Autoliv said.
Production in the European car industry -- which Autoliv says is its most important market -- had been two percent higher than in the same 1995 period, Autoliv said.
However, car specification upgrades meant an eight percent increase in airbag sales to four billion crowns, whilst sales of car seatbelts rose 12 percent to 4.6 billion crowns.
In September, Autoliv announced it had signed a letter of intent with Morton International to create the world's largest specialist manufacturer of airbags and other car safety equipment.
The new company, Autoliv Inc, will have an annual turnover of 20 billion crowns and 15,000 employees.
A final deal is to be signed in November and, subject to the approval of competition authorities, an offer prospectus will be published next spring, Autoliv said.
Autoliv's share price moved little on the result. At 1220 GMT its shares were 0.5 crowns higher at 284 crowns.
A Reuter poll of eight analysts found an average forecast for a profit after financial items of 870 million crowns. ($ = 6.579 Swedish Crowns)
